key_insight: AEAPTMS amino-silane passivation makes mixed-halide perovskite surfaces more electronically uniform and stable, reducing grain-boundary potential barriers while boosting and speeding surface photovoltage response.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical route to lower photovoltage losses and improve carrier uniformity in perovskite solar cells through molecular surface engineering.
method: Amplitude-modulated Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) to map dark CPD and illuminated SPV at the nanoscale.
Compare passivated vs. unpassivated mixed-cation, mixed-halide perovskite thin films.
Separate grain-boundary and grain-interior contributions and probe wavelength-dependent SPV to assess disorder.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports CPD distribution narrowing from ~45.7 to ~14.6 mV, SPV increasing from ~345 to ~417 mV, and the stabilisation time constant dropping from ~840 to ~470 s after AEAPTMS treatment.
watch_item: KPFM results are surface-sensitive and film-level, so the passivation gains should be validated against full-device stability and reproducibility under operational conditions.
paper_title: Understanding surface potential dynamics of passivated perovskites via Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
